claims.text: Premelting in Fe–Ni–Cr–Co–Cu high-entropy-alloy nanoparticles initiates at free surfaces.
Local chemical segregation at free surfaces initiates premelting.
Cu is a lower-melting component whose local enrichment or depletion is especially relevant to premelting.
Surface chemical segregation locally reduces cohesive energy.
The local reduction in cohesive energy triggers atomic disordering.
An ultrathin amorphous-silica coating suppresses surface atomic mobility and limits chemical segregation.
Suppressing surface mobility and segregation with the coating raises the premelting-onset temperature relative to uncoated particles.
The surface energy landscape and intrinsic local chemical ordering, particularly the distribution of Cu, govern the onset of atomic disordering.
Unconstrained free surfaces facilitate early atomic mobility and chemical segregation.
Early atomic mobility and segregation cause an early local loss of crystalline order.
A silica coating changes the surface boundary condition by limiting surface diffusion.
Limiting surface diffusion delays surface-induced segregation and nucleation of disordered phases.
Coated particles will exhibit a higher premelting-onset temperature than uncoated particles.
Coated particles will exhibit less pronounced or delayed elemental segregation, especially of Cu.
Coated particles will undergo a more gradual melting transition than uncoated particles.
The proposed mechanism applies to particles in the 5–20 nm diameter range from premelting onset through complete melting under inert or high-vacuum conditions.
The proposed mechanism may not apply to larger particles or reactive environments involving oxidation or other chemical interactions.
